problem: Judge LLMs differ substantially in reliability, so treating all judges equally when evaluating LLMs via pairwise comparisons yields biased leaderboards and misleading uncertainty estimates.
approach: Extend the Bradley-Terry-Luce model by introducing judge-specific discrimination parameters to jointly estimate latent model quality and judge reliability from pairwise comparisons without reference labels.
contribution: The framework achieves identifiability and consistency with asymptotic normality of the MLE, improving agreement with human preferences and producing calibrated uncertainty quantification for LLM rankings.

problem: Online RL for LLM alignment is unstable under noisy rewards due to directional inconsistency: high-reward rollouts within a batch induce representation-space preference directions that sharply disagree with the batch majority.
approach: GeoAlign curates rollouts by learning an online projector on per-rollout hidden states to detect and rectify directionally inconsistent rollouts via angular deviation from a batch consensus prototype.
contribution: GeoAlign improves final performance and reduces training oscillation across dialogue alignment and mathematical reasoning tasks, outperforming PF-PPO, PAR, PODS, and Seed-GRPO.

problem: Vision-language models lack ability to adapt their decision criteria in response to criterion shifts while maintaining fixed task semantics, a common requirement in real-world applications.
approach: Introduce Criterion-Conditional In-Context Learning (CC-ICL) with dual-level data hierarchy and metrics (Criterion Invariance and Criterion Sensitivity) to evaluate robustness and adaptability under criterion shifts.
contribution: Most MLLMs exhibit rigid boundary bias; simple multi-criterion training significantly improves Criterion Sensitivity, enabling 7B-scale models to surpass proprietary models.

problem: It remains unclear how audio deepfake detection capability scales with model capacity and training data under realistic deployment conditions involving distribution shift, signal corruption, and unseen synthesis pipelines.
approach: Present the first systematic study of scaling laws in post-training audio deepfake detection by analyzing performance, robustness, and generalization as functions of model size and training data scale.
contribution: Reveal a fundamental asymmetry between performance scaling and robustness scaling, showing that increasing model capacity alone is insufficient for achieving reliable real-world generalization.

problem: Training and deploying separate models with different capabilities for access control is prohibitively expensive, yet a single model shared across users can enable dual-use misuse.
approach: Propose Gradient-Routed Auxiliary Modules (GRAM), a pre-training method that adds modules and selectively updates them to induce specialization; ablating a module at inference time removes its capability.
contribution: GRAM preserves retain capabilities while disabling forgotten capabilities, limits recovery better than post-hoc unlearning, and achieves 5x cost reduction for 5-profile settings with Chinchilla-optimal scaling.

problem: Low-rank approximation for model compression and parameter-efficient fine-tuning overlooks shifts in feature distributions, leading to error amplification and unstable inference.
approach: Propose distribution-aware whitening framework that dynamically whitens layer inputs based on evolving feature distributions to ensure second-order isotropy, minimizing cumulative approximation errors.
contribution: Achieves tighter control over layerwise distortion in post-training compression and serves as effective initialization for LoRA-style parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

problem: Finetuning VLA models with RL is constrained by high cost and safety risks of real-world interaction; training in world models introduces challenges including pixel-level modeling, multi-view consistency, and compounding errors.
approach: Propose VLA-MBPO with three key design choices: (i) unified multimodal models for data-efficient world modeling, (ii) interleaved view decoding for multi-view consistency, (iii) chunk-level branched rollout to mitigate error compounding.
contribution: VLA-MBPO significantly improves policy performance and sample efficiency on simulation and real-world tasks while maintaining universal hyperparameters across all tasks.

problem: Metaphorical videos convey complex ideas requiring high-order cognitive capabilities, but current MLLMs struggle with metaphorical understanding due to defective cross-domain mapping.
approach: Construct MetaphorVU-Bench benchmark for evaluating metaphorical video understanding and propose MetaphorBoost, an inference-time enhancement using metaphor knowledge graph as mapping augmentation.
contribution: MetaphorBoost achieves consistent performance improvement and provides insights for advancing MLLMs' metaphorical comprehension capabilities.

problem: Continuous Normalizing Flows require costly iterative sampling and lack interpretability of intermediate states; existing acceleration methods treat the generative process as a black box.
approach: Globally linearize flow dynamics via Koopman theory to achieve trajectory-preserving linearization by lifting Conditional Flow Matching into a higher-dimensional Koopman space with a single linear operator.
contribution: Sampling becomes one-step and parallelizable with unique insights on generation; enables semantic editing direction discovery, inversion with teacher-aligned operator, and spectral analysis of trajectories.

problem: Self-consistency methods suffer from high computation cost by evaluating output consistency monolithically and using static stopping criteria that cannot adapt to varying task complexities and model capabilities.
approach: Present Task-and-Model-Aware Fractal-Consistency (TMAFC) with Fractal-Consistency evaluating consistency at component granularity and Adaptive Stopping Criteria Calibration dynamically adjusting based on task and model assessment.
contribution: TMAFC reduces sample cost by up to 55% while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Data heterogeneity in Federated Learning induces model drift resulting in negative gains where global models perform worse than local training on data-abundant clients.
approach: Propose FedGain, a framework that optimizes collaborative client clustering by developing a modified Scaling Law to quantify data utility reduction and defining Effective Federated Capacity.
contribution: FedGain effectively suppresses negative gains to negligible levels across various FL algorithms and outperforms other Clustered FL methods.

problem: Designing heuristic algorithms for complex optimization is time-consuming and expert-driven; existing Automated Heuristic Design using LLMs relies on task-specific programs that fail to generalize.
approach: Introduce Multi-Task Hierarchical Search (MTHS), an LLM-guided evolutionary method that co-designs general-purpose metaheuristics and task-specific programs with hierarchical representation and two-level evolution.
contribution: MTHS outperforms both commonly-used heuristics and existing LLM-driven AHD approaches, with evolved metaheuristics exhibiting strong generalization to related tasks.

problem: Causal discovery typically relies on strong assumptions like non-Gaussianity; modern applications with multiple related views of the same system have rarely been leveraged for causal discovery.
approach: Propose multi-view linear Structural Equation Model extending non-Gaussian disturbances framework by leveraging correlation across views; prove identifiability for acyclic SEMs.
contribution: Multi-view methods inspired by DirectLiNGAM, PairwiseLiNGAM, and ICA-LiNGAM enable causal graph estimation from neuroimaging data.

problem: Vision-Language Pre-trained models are vulnerable to real-world query noise; current Test-Time Adaptation methods rely on high-confidence predictions, inducing confirmation bias and neglecting informative ambiguous queries.
approach: Propose ReEx framework with Generative Semantic Refinement for textual structural noise correction via Confidence-Guided Dynamic Fusion and Exclusion-Guided Proxy Contrastive Learning exploiting ambiguous data.
contribution: ReEx consistently outperforms existing TTA methods on COCO-C and Flickr-C with significant robustness gains.

problem: Prior latent dynamics identifiability results condition on pre-defined environment labels, hindering generalization to unseen environments and limiting understanding of dynamics function and environment variable identifiability.
approach: Propose Meta-iLaD using meta-learning across dynamics environments with a conditional prior modeled as a feedforward meta-learner to extract environment variables from few-shot examples.
contribution: Establishes simultaneous identifiability for latent states, environment variables, and dynamics function; enables generalization to out-of-distribution environments with improved forecasting.

problem: Asynchronous RL for LLM post-training introduces distributional mismatch between data from stale policies and the current policy, causing unstable training and degraded performance.
approach: Propose D-ARL, a framework that selects high-quality asynchronous samples whose distributions align with the current policy using variance-guided metrics and maintains a replay buffer of recent samples.
contribution: D-ARL achieves average improvement of 6.4% in reasoning performance and 34.7% in sample efficiency over state-of-the-art asynchronous methods.

problem: Graph neural networks remain vulnerable to out-of-distribution shifts in node features and graph structure; models capture spurious signals leaving them fragile under distributional changes.
approach: Propose TIDE, a Tri-Component Information Decomposition framework that explicitly decomposes information into feature-specific, structure-specific and joint components using information bottleneck objectives.
contribution: TIDE achieves up to 34% improvement in FPR95 over strong baselines while maintaining competitive ID accuracy on graph OOD detection.

problem: Generating large-scale high-quality datasets for training PDE solvers is computationally expensive; deep learning methods remain constrained by substantial computational costs despite high-performance computing.
approach: Introduce Neural-HSS, a parameter-efficient architecture built upon Hierarchical Semi-Separable matrix structure inspired by Green's functions for elliptic PDEs.
contribution: Neural-HSS is provably data-efficient for broad PDE classes, outperforms baselines on 3D Poisson equation and demonstrates capability on diverse applications in electromagnetism, fluid dynamics, and biology.

problem: Generative world models for autonomous driving suffer from three gaps: history-incompatible initialization, sampling latency exceeding real-time budgets, and compounding kinematic infeasibility.
approach: Propose VectorWorld, a streaming vector-graph world model with motion-aware gated VAE for initialization, edge-gated relational DiT with MeanFlow for solver-free outpainting, and ΔSim for physics-aligned NPC policy.
contribution: VectorWorld improves map fidelity, initialization validity, and density calibration, enabling stable real-time 1km+ closed-loop rollouts on Waymo and nuPlan.

problem: The interaction between stepsize, batch size, and stochastic noise in stochastic conditional gradient methods lacks explicit theoretical understanding, hindering efficient large-scale training design.
approach: Study momentum-based stochastic Frank-Wolfe algorithms under Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz condition to derive analysis capturing stepsize, batch size, and noise interactions; predict optimal batch size magnitude.
contribution: Theory reveals regime-dependent batch size behavior and aligns with empirical practices; provides principled batch size and stepsize selection guidelines with adaptive strategies.

problem: Fine-tuning generators to reduce classifier filtering probability pushes models toward decision boundaries, increasing false positives and negatives rather than improving safety.
approach: Propose Boundary Guidance, an RL fine-tuning method that explicitly steers generation away from the classifier's decision margin using reinforcement learning.
contribution: Boundary Guidance improves safety while maintaining or improving utility on jailbreak, ambiguous, and long-context prompts as judged by LLM-as-a-Judge.

problem: Computer architecture remains absent from current LLM evaluations despite being a domain requiring high-order thinking; existing benchmarks do not assess architectural reasoning.
approach: Present QuArch, a benchmark with 2,671 expert-validated QA pairs covering processor design, memory systems, and interconnection networks; evaluate frontier models on analysis, design, and implementation questions.
contribution: Frontier model accuracies vary widely (34% to 73%) on advanced questions; fine-tuning on QuArch improves memory hierarchy design task performance up to 1.99x.

problem: Text-attributed graphs face data uncertainty in open-world environments with limited labels; existing approaches optimize semantics or topology in isolation, failing to integrate textual and structural information.
approach: Introduce Open-world Graph Assistant (OGA), an LLM-based framework with Adaptive Label Traceability for unknown-class rejection and Graph Label Annotator for unknown-class annotation.
contribution: OGA automates handling of unlabeled nodes in open-world environments, enabling model updates and long-term deployment with effective unknown-class detection.

problem: Standard model stitching for functional similarity evaluation is blind to invariance properties, allowing models relying on different information cues to appear misleadingly similar.
approach: Introduce invariance-aware model stitching that enforces forward-backward compatibility requirement, analyzing interplay between forward and backward compatibility.
contribution: Invariance-aware model stitching provides principled approach to functional similarity evaluation while revealing functional discrepancies previously obscured.

problem: Extended reasoning in MLLMs plateaus as the model locks into specific thinking patterns; horizontal scaling via parallel reasoning faces open questions in visual domain.
approach: Propose Visual Para-Thinker, a parallel reasoning framework for MLLMs with visual partitioning strategies, Pa-Attention for path independence, and LPRoPE for diversity promotion.
contribution: Visual Para-Thinker successfully extends parallel reasoning benefits to visual domain with high-efficiency multimodal implementation via vLLM.

problem: Large kernel convolutions for 3D volumetric analysis suffer optimization instability; naively increasing kernel size leads to convergence issues.
approach: Propose Rep3D, a framework employing lightweight modulation networks to generate receptive-biased scaling masks that adaptively re-weight kernel updates.
contribution: Rep3D consistently outperforms transformer and fixed-prior baselines on five 3D segmentation benchmarks using plain encoder architecture.

problem: Test-time scaling through Chain-of-Thought succeeds but whether computational steps during pretraining can improve per-token generation remains unclear.
approach: Propose PonderLM-2, a pretraining methodology where LM generates intermediate latent thought (last hidden state) before predicting subsequent token, enabling continuous-space refinement.
contribution: At identical inference cost, PonderLM-2-Pythia-1.4B significantly outperforms vanilla Pythia-2.8B on language modeling and downstream tasks; increasing latent thoughts improves performance.

problem: Inferring dynamical evolution from limited observations requires trajectory simulation at inference time, making inference a bottleneck for scalable single-cell applications.
approach: Propose Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Mean Flow Matching (WFR-MFM), a mean-flow framework that summarizes transport and mass-growth dynamics using mean velocity and mass-growth fields.
contribution: WFR-MFM achieves orders-of-magnitude faster inference than baselines while maintaining accuracy; enables efficient perturbation response prediction on large datasets.

problem: Self-supervised learning methods align continuous features without control over representation structure; most methods offer limited insight into learned representations.
approach: Frame visual SSL as discrete communication between teacher and student networks through binary channel; student predicts multi-label binary messages with binary cross-entropy loss.
contribution: Discrete agreement with coding-rate regularization and periodic projection head reinitialization produces structured, compact discrete language; improves classification, retrieval, and domain shift robustness.

problem: LLM-as-a-judge exhibits translationese bias where models systematically favor machine-translated text over human-authored references, especially in low-resource languages.
approach: Present DIBJudge, a fine-tuning framework that disentangles robust features and bias representations via explicit bias branch and vector-quantized compression for minimal sufficient information.
contribution: DIBJudge mitigates translationese bias and outperforms strong baselines on multilingual reward modeling and bias evaluation benchmarks.

problem: Determining where to execute manipulation policy is formulated as geometric search prioritizing reachability, but optimal performance requires base positioning aware of policy preference.
approach: Introduce N2M that learns policy preferences from rollouts; proposes viewpoint augmentation strategy enabling robust, viewpoint-invariant pose preference learning.
contribution: N2M achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming policy-aware alternatives with broad applicability, strong generalization, and remarkable data efficiency.

problem: Developing zero-shot time series anomaly detection models that generalize to unseen data remains challenging; reconstruction-error scoring misses subtle anomalies.
approach: Introduce TimeRCD, a foundation model built on Relative Context Discrepancy enabling anomaly detection via pattern comparison with surrounding context rather than fixed global patterns.
contribution: TimeRCD outperforms existing foundation models in most zero-shot TSAD settings while remaining competitive with dataset-specific baselines.

problem: Predicting spatial gene expression overlooks essential biological structures like gene coordination and spatial distribution, treating tasks as isolated pointwise problems.
approach: Introduce FLAG, a diffusion-based framework for structured distribution modeling with spatial graph encoder for topological consistency and Gene Foundation Model alignment.
contribution: FLAG achieves competitive traditional accuracy while demonstrating enhanced structural fidelity with novel metrics (GSC/SSC) capturing gene-gene and gene-spatial relationships.

problem: Understanding how neural networks change topological invariants through layers and comparing expressivity of different architectures requires controlled low-dimensional analysis.
approach: Study layered models by limiting each layer width to d=3 (ℝ³ representation space) enabling visualization and tracking topological invariants including linking numbers through layers.
contribution: Prove ResNet layer-skipping and transformer attention match in power for affecting linking numbers; both strictly more powerful than feedforward networks but require nonmonotonic activations.

problem: Portfolio optimization with transaction costs lacks models considering both transaction costs and sparsity simultaneously, with NP-hardness from K-sparse constraints complicating solutions.
approach: Propose K-sparse transaction cost model reformulated as nonsmooth difference of convex optimization; develop Proximal Subgradient Algorithm with ADMM for proximity operator computation.
contribution: Establish global convergence and R-linear convergence rate via Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property with KL exponent 1/2.

problem: GP-TS analysis for Bayesian optimization lacks high-probability regret bounds and it remains unclear whether recent GP-UCB improvements apply to GP-TS.
approach: Provide regret lower bound for GP-TS and derive multiple upper bounds including second moment of cumulative regret, expected lenient regret, and improved cumulative regret bounds.
contribution: Show GP-TS suffers polynomial dependence on 1/δ with probability δ; provide improved regret bounds on time horizon T matching theoretical structure.

problem: Training Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks lacks principled theory for training dynamics, generalization, and privacy properties compared to standard MLPs.
approach: Analyze gradient descent for two-layer KANs with specialization to logistic loss under NTK-separable assumption; derive bounds characterizing optimization, generalization, and differential privacy.
contribution: Show polylogarithmic width suffices for 1/T optimization and 1/n generalization; identify qualitative gap between non-private and private training regimes revealing polylogarithmic width necessity.

problem: Large language models allocate uniform computation across tokens despite variable predictability; some sequences are trivially easy while others require deep reasoning.
approach: Introduce ConceptMoE which dynamically merges semantically similar tokens into concepts via learnable chunking; MoE enables isolated evaluation of architectural benefits.
contribution: ConceptMoE achieves +0.9 points on pretraining, +2.3 on long context, +0.6 on multimodal; reduces attention computation R²x, KV cache Rx with 175% prefill and 117% decoding speedups.

problem: The role of the critic in entropy-regularized actor-critic remains underexplored; variance reduction and convergence guarantees depend critically on critic accuracy.
approach: Study actor-critic for entropy-regularized finite discounted environments; establish that exact critic acts as variance-reduction baseline and analyze performance with learned but approximate critic.
contribution: With exact critic matches sample complexity of deterministic policy gradient reaching epsilon-optimal solution with Õ(log(1/ε)) samples; identify importance of accurate critic learning.

problem: PINNs train slowly or fail on challenging PDEs due to severely ill-conditioned loss landscapes inherited from the underlying differential operator.
approach: Study PINNs augmented with pointwise data-fidelity supervision; propose FK-PINNs using Feynman-Kac functional Monte Carlo labels and show operator-level preconditioning effect.
contribution: Derive non-asymptotic L²(Ω)-error bounds for FK-PINNs; establish pseudo-dimension bounds for tanh network derivatives; demonstrate successful solutions on PDEs where standard PINNs fail.
